transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Lunaris), Ethan Park (Lunaris), Sofia Ribeiro (Lunaris)

Summary: cost/unit econ review; cache + batching tuning items; next steps agreed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda - cost model walk, benchmark notes, and next steps.
[00:12] Maya: thanks, yeah we want to focus on tokens per dollar and where caching helps for our conversational flows.
[00:20] Carlos: cool, i pulled last week's runs. note: the 2k seq baseline on the hosted endpoint gave us ~1,200 tokens/sec at p50, with cost around $0.0021 per 1k tokens — rough numbers.
[00:35] Ethan: sorry can you repeat the tokens/sec per dollar part? our finance wants tokens/sec/$ not just cost per 1k.
[00:40] Jamie: yeah, good point. so roughly converted that's about 0.6M tokens per dollar at the baseline config, but that varies a lot with batch size and cache hit rate.
[01:05] Carlos: and importantly, when we enable prefix KV caching with our 70% prefix reuse from your sample prompts, we saw effective tokens/sec/$ jump by ~2.3x on our internal runs — that's with bs=16 and async batching.
[01:25] Sofia: 70% reuse seems high for some flows, i think our control plane has some longer unique contexts so maybe 50% on real traffic.
[01:35] Maya: yeah we measure 55-60% reuse on search-assist, but customer chat is lower. we'll share distributions.
[01:45] Carlos: perfect — that distribution will let us run more realistic cache sims. also note tradeoff: larger batch sizes improve tokens/sec but increase tail latency. in our tests bs=32 increased throughput by ~30% vs bs=8 but 95th latency jumped from 220ms to 420ms on the hosted config.
[02:15] Ethan: our SLO is 300ms p95 for interactive features, so bs=32 would break that.
[02:22] Jamie: that's where Dedicated comes in — with reserved capacity you can push bigger batches and keep tail lower. Carlos, remind them numbers for Dedicated?
[02:30] Carlos: on Dedicated GPUs with optimized kernels and 4k KV cache, we saw ~1.8x throughput vs hosted at same batch size, and p95 stayed under 280ms for bs=24 in our synthetic. cost per token went down ~20% after you amortize reserved capacity.
[02:50] Maya: amortize reserved - can you send a model of the commit levels? we need to see monthly vs on-demand breakeven.
[03:00] Jamie: yes, i'll post the cost spreadsheet, it's got break-even curves for commits at 0.5/1/2/4k tokens per second sustained.
[03:10] Sofia: curious about quantization impact — does 8-bit cause accuracy diffs for our NLU tasks?
[03:16] Carlos: short answer: small drop for some generative tasks, but for reranking/embeddings it's minimal. for your NLU intents we ran a eval and accuracy drop was within noise for 8-bit dynamic quant on the smaller models, but for very long context generative outputs we saw occasional degens. we can pin a higher-precision variant for those routes.
[03:40] Ethan: networking question — if we go Dedicated in our VPC, what's the peering setup? we need zero-egress policies.
[03:46] Jamie: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link; we can do egress controls and customer-managed encryption keys. we'll include network diagram in the security pack.
[03:55] Carlos: action items: i'll run the 4k seq KV-cache bench with bs=8,16,32 and share raw figures. note: expect cache hit patterns to change the metrics a lot; please send the prompt reuse histogram.
[04:10] Maya: i'll upload prompt distro and a few representative sessions to the drive.
[04:16] Jamie: note on tokens/sec/$ formula in the sheet: we include compute cost + storage amortization + network. it's annotated.
[04:24] Sofia: for POC success criteria — we need cost per active user <$0.05 and p95 latency <300ms for 80% of traffic.
[04:33] Carlos: okay we can model that — two levers: cache hit rate and batch sizing; also model multi-tier fallback to cheaper quantized models for low-criticality tasks.
[04:45] Ethan: any competitors do prefix caching like this out of box?
[04:48] Jamie: some vendors offer caching but not with tight SLO controls + Dedicated autoscale; Anthropic/OpenAI - varies, and seldon is more infra-level. we'll put competitive notes in the follow-up.
[05:02] Carlos: also quick caution - the benchmark logs had occasional transcription mismatch in our run scripts — some labels were off, so i'll re-run and sanity check the token accounting.
[05:12] Maya: preference is raw CSVs so our infra team can ingest them.
[05:16] Carlos: will do.
[05:20] Jamie: recap: Carlos runs kv/cache 4k bench (bs 8/16/32) and shares CSV; Jamie shares cost model and security pack; Lunaris shares prompt distro and SLOs; schedule infra deep-dive. agreed?
[05:34] All: yes / thanks
[05:38] Jamie: okay i'll send calendar invite for the infra deep-dive and add notes. thanks everyone.
